title: Runtime semver policy, staged-flag rollouts, and automated migration CLI
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: define and operationalize a clear runtime semantic versioning policy and supporting rollout/migration tooling so that breaking changes are predictable, discoverable, and automatable across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. This ticket consolidates policy, rollout gates, deprecation windows, and the MVP spec for an Automated Migration CLI (amcli) that will scan client usage, surface incompatibilities, and optionally generate migration patches or SDK upgrade guidance.
rationale: We continue to observe friction when changing runtime behavior that customers depend on (KV cache eviction semantics, inference API minor shape changes, tokenization differences). Ambiguous versioning and inconsistent deprecation metadata cause costly rollbacks, support lift, and delayed adoption of improvements. A formal semver policy + tooling reduces risk, shortens migration paths, and enables more aggressive optimization in the runtime without surprising users.
scope: This policy covers public request/response shapes, HTTP headers, core runtime behaviors (KV cache, batching semantics, model variant compatibility), and SDK-visible defaults. It excludes purely internal observability fields and behind-the-scenes scheduling improvements that do not change API contracts.
policy_principles: 1) Consumers choose a compatibility channel (LTS/stable/edge). 2) Breaking changes require a major bump and documented migration path. 3) Deprecations are signaled with a standard header and minimum 90-day window for Hosted, 180-day for Dedicated, and 365-day for Private where customers opt-out of auto-upgrades. 4) Runtime releases must include a machine-readable compatibility manifest. 5) Provide automated tooling to detect and assist migration.
breaking_change_criteria: A change is 'breaking' if it causes an unhandled client error, meaning any previously valid request may start to fail or return semantically different outputs (e.g., removing a top-level field, changing required parameters, altering tokenization behavior that affects logits). Examples: renaming top-level 'generated_text' to 'output_text' -> breaking. Increasing the positional index of a required argument -> breaking. Adjusting a default from 'true' to 'false' that changes response shape -> breaking if callers depend on previous default.
deprecation_signal: All deprecated endpoints/features must emit an 'X-Redwood-Deprecation: v<target-version>; sunset=<YYYY-MM-DD>; reason=<short>' response header and a deprecation entry in the compatibility manifest. The Console will show deprecation alerts and the amcli will surface occurrences in customer projects.
lts_and_channels: Channels: edge (fast, experimental), stable (regular releases, semver-minor safe), LTS (predictable, security/bug fixes only). LTS cadence: 12 months supported with backported security fixes; customers may pin a runtime LTS minor. Minor bumps are allowed for additive, backwards-compatible features; major bumps indicate breaking changes and will only be released with a migration plan and extended support window.
rollout_gates: 1) CI: compatibility smoke test suite against pinned example apps. 2) Canary: 1% of traffic for 48 hours with synthetic and real-user monitoring. 3) Telemetry thresholds: error rate, latency, and quality regression metrics (automatic rollback if >3 sigma above baseline for 30m). 4) Manual approval by release owner if any compatibility warnings present. 5) Gradual ramping: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with at least 6 hours between ramps and passing health checks.
compatibility_manifest_spec: A JSON manifest included in each runtime release describing: released_version, semantic_level (major/minor/patch), public_endpoints_and_shapes (list of stable fields+types), deprecated_entries (field, deprecated_in_version, sunset_date, migration_notes), optional_feature_flags, and binary_compatibility_tags. The Console and amcli will consume this manifest.
migration_tool_spec: amcli MVP features: 1) 'amcli scan --url <endpoint> --token <secret>' to run an inventory of calls made by a repository or recorded traffic, 2) map discovered usage to compatibility manifest entries, 3) produce a 'migration-report.md' with prioritized actions, 4) optional 'amcli patch --suggest' to apply safe code-mods for common SDK patterns (rename fields, switch config flags), 5) prebuilt recipes for SDKs (python/js/go) that generate PR templates and test stubs. The tool will also export a JSON report consumable by CI.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Semver policy doc reviewed and approved by Release Engineering, API Platform, and Developer Experience. 2) Compatibility manifest schema committed and validated by runtime build. 3) Canary + telemetry gating added to release pipeline. 4) amcli MVP can scan a small sample repo and produce a migration report with at least 80% precision on detectable field renames. 5) Documentation and a Console deprecation UI prototype exist.
implementation_steps: 1) Draft policy and get stakeholder signoff (week 1). 2) Implement compatibility manifest generation in runtime build (week 2-3). 3) Add deprecation header to runtime responses (week 2). 4) Instrument release pipeline with staged canary and telemetry checks (week 3-4). 5) Build amcli MVP (week 3-6): scanner + report generator + SDK recipes. 6) Run internal migration drills on 3 reference apps and tune thresholds (week 6-7). 7) Public docs and Console alerting (week 7-8).
testing_and_validation: - Create a suite of regression scenarios (tokenization, field rename, default flip) and include in compatibility tests. - Use internal reference apps for canary trials. - Add unit tests for manifest generation and manifest consumers. - Evaluate amcli reports against ground-truth migrations from previous incidents.
monitoring_and_rollback: Define health metrics: 5xx rate, median latency, model-quality delta for top-10 prompts, SDK error telemetry. Rollback triggers: sustained 5xx > 0.5% above baseline for 15m, model-quality drop > 2% on sentinel evals, customer-impacting errors reported via support. Document manual rollback playbook and automate rollback in pipeline when triggers exceed thresholds.
privacy_and_compliance_considerations: amcli scanning is opt-in. For Hosted customers we will scan sandbox/test traffic only unless explicit consent granted. For Dedicated/Private, provide an offline mode where amcli runs inside customer network without telemetry export. Ensure migration reports strip PII and include guidance on local execution.
risks: - False positives/negatives from amcli causing developer distrust. - Customers on Private infra may not accept shorter deprecation windows. - Compatibility manifest omissions leading to silent breakages. Mitigations: conservative default behavior, extended private windows, and mandatory integration tests before major releases.
open_questions: 1) Should we include binary layout guarantees for native extensions? 2) What is the exact sunset duration for security-only LTS patches? 3) How aggressive should amcli auto-patch be vs. only suggesting PRs?
notes: This ticket focuses on policy and the amcli MVP. Separate follow-ups will cover SDK-level adapters, long-term telemetry enrichment, and commercial communications for large Dedicated/Private customers. Track those as successor issues after policy signoff.
next_steps: Schedule a 1-hour review with Release Engineering and DevEx week of 2026-03-15; assign a PM owner for customer comms and create ENG tasks for manifest integration and amcli subcomponents.
